definition: An uncertainty factor is an influence that makes outcomes harder to predict, such as changing climate conditions in crop production. In a cognition context, it is something people take into account when judging risk and making later planning decisions.

reasons: The packet supports an agricultural/climate-risk sense of “uncertainty factor” (climate variability in crop production), not the added cognition-specific sense about how people judge risk and make planning decisions.

The definition includes an example (“changing climate conditions in crop production”) that aligns with the packet’s “climate variability,” but because the cognition-related generalization is not adequately supported, the overall definition is not fully defensible from the supplied source text.
